problems.field: studies[S1].participants.country (paper_design_summary repeats it: 'students at UNAM (Mexico City)')
problems.source_says: The paper never names the students' university or the place of the workshop. UNAM appears only in the two authors' affiliations. Section 3.1 says only that design teachers recruited the students and that the academic authorities of the bachelor program approved the study. One remark about the sketch ideas implies Mexico City. Suggested value: 'Mexico (Mexico City implied, p. 6; the paper does not name the university, and both authors are at UNAM)'. This is a wording fix. No count changes.
problems.quote: related to students’ everyday experiences (for example, solutions around the “tinaco”, a water container and characteristic element of Mexico City dwellings)
problems.locator: p. 6, Section 4.2.1; p. 1, author affiliations; p. 3, Section 3.1

problems.form_value: 'No participant exclusions are stated for the design task.' The field then lists only subsets smaller than 61 (42 questionnaire respondents, 27 of 30 AI logs).
problems.source_says: The one count above 61 is missing from this field. The AUT range groups sum to 25 + 36 + 7 = 68, seven more than the 61 participants. The paper does not explain the gap or say when the four groups were randomized relative to the diagnostic phase. It may be a typo, or seven students may have taken the AUT but not the design task. The form records the sum only in notes. The explicit counts at assignment (31 and 30) still support n_randomized = 61, so the field needs one added sentence, not a new count.
problems.quote: If we distribute students into three groups, we obtain 25 in the high range (3,1- 5), 36 in the mid-range (2,1-3) and 7 in the lower range (1-2).

confirmed.statement: 61 people took part: industrial design bachelor students in their 8th semester, 38 female and 23 male (38 + 23 = 61), ages 21 to 30. The abstract and introduction repeat 61.
confirmed.locator: p. 3, Section 3.1; p. 1, Abstract and Section 1

confirmed.statement: n_randomized 61 (arms 31 and 30): four student groups were randomly assigned to sketch groups A+C (n=31) and AI groups B+D (n=30).
n_analyzed 61 (arms 31 and 30): the rated set held 71 ideas from the sketch group (n=31 students) and 44 ideas from the AI groups (n=30 students), and Section 4.2.3 repeats 31 and 30 students.
The printed per-person fluency means use 31 and 30 as divisors: 71/31 = 2.29 (printed 2.2), 44/30 = 1.47 (1.4), 89/31 = 2.87 (2.8), 291/30 = 9.70 (9.7).

The per-participant correlations fit the arm sizes. Recomputed from the printed r and p, the AI-arm creativity correlation (r = -.30, p = .103) fits only n = 30 or 31, so all 30 AI students had a rated idea. The sketch-arm correlations (r = .12, p = .54 and .53) fit n = 26 to 32, which includes 31.

The form's counts are people, not ideas. The n = 54, 24, 17, and 20 in the t-tests are ideas: they sum to the 115 rated items, t(76) has df = 54 + 24 - 2, and one sketch group cannot hold 54 people when the arm has 31. Table 1's n=71 and n=44 are ideas too. The form keeps all of these out of the people counts (S1-O1 n_units 115).
confirmed.locator: p. 6, Table 1 and Section 4.2.1; p. 5, Section 3.2.3

confirmed.statement: Other AI-arm counts fit 30 people: 18 of 30 students had the light-ring concept, and 28 of 30 made images from an LLM-written prompt. Some subgroup lists do not sum to the arm size (AI design paths 22 + 7 + 3 = 32, LLM users 23 + 2 + 3 + 3 + 1 = 32, prompt styles 13 + 7 + 6 = 26 of 27 logs). The paper does not explain these sums, though some students switched models (path C, n=3). The form notes the path and prompt sums. None of these overrides the explicit 31 and 30.

confirmed.statement: The authors' other candidate paper (c898, ICED 2025, doi 10.1017/pds.2025.10055) reports, per its publisher page, a workshop with 19 architecture bachelor and industrial design master students in 8 teams and no no-AI group, so it does not share this sample. A web search found no other report of the April 2025 workshop.
confirmed.locator: Cambridge Core page for c898, read 2026-10-05; candidates.json entry c898

confirmed.statement: Criterion 2 holds: one randomized study analyzed 61 people (31 + 30), above 50. Assignment was by four groups, which bears on precision but not on the people count.

summary: The participant counts are right: four student groups were randomly assigned with 31 sketch and 30 AI students, the same 61 people were analyzed, and the idea counts, per-person means, and AI-arm correlation all fit them, with no reported attrition, second study, or shared sample. The refutation rests on two details outside the counts (the form names UNAM as the site, which the paper never states, and the exclusions field leaves out the unexplained AUT total of 68), so criterion 2 holds with 61 people analyzed.
